newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian civil servants to strike over job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Australian civil servants to strike over job cuts.

text.p: Thousands of Australian civil servants will begin a second round of strikes around the country from Tuesday to protest against government cutbacks, a key union leader said on Friday.

Commonwealth Public Sector Union national secretary Wendy Caird told Reuters that union members voted on Friday to continue their programme of 12-hour strikes against the government over job cuts and attacks on employment conditions.
"There will be rolling strikes from Tuesday -- and that means they will be in a different state each day over two weeks," Caird said.
The union rejected the government's decision to cut civil service jobs by 16,500, announced in the 1997/98 budget on Tuesday.
"If we haven't had any changes in the government's position after this round then we will consider another round based on agency stoppages," she said.
Civil servants protested against government cutbacks in a first round of two hour strikes on a state-by state basis at the beginning of May.
The union represents 60,000 of Australia's 130,000 federal public servants.
